Sofia (Sales Eng): Hey team, pilot customer Velocity just reported a sudden spike in 504s over the last 10 minutes and token usage doubled. They’re on a Dedicated trial, traffic ~2k rps now. Can we triage?
Ben (Account Exec): On call with their infra lead, they're worried about cost and SLA. Asked for ETA to stabilize.
Maya (Oncall): I'm pulling logs now. Any recent rollout?
Raj (Infra): No scheduled deploys from infra side. Checking autoscaler events and GPU health.
Alex (SRE): I see a pattern of long tail latencies hitting one backend pool. Might be KV cache pressure causing large KV loads. Can someone paste sample logs?
Sofia (Sales Eng): Pasting sanitized request/response snippet from customer chat: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-7b","prompt":"...","max_tokens":1024}'
Response: HTTP 504 after 18s, server logs: 
[2026-03-20T15:12:09Z] request_id=abc123 pool=dedicated-gpu-7b latency=18.1s status=504 kv_miss=1 batch_size=1
[2026-03-20T15:12:09Z] runtime: kv_cache_evictions=128 mem_pressure=0.87
```
Maya (Oncall): kv_cache_evictions that high points to cache eviction storm. If caches are thrashing, long token-generation times possible. Raj, can you confirm memory metrics on that pool?
Raj (Infra): Looking at node metrics: GPU mem usage steady but host RSS spikes. I see a cron job for nightly model warmup that started ~15:00 UTC — could be overlapping. Scaling events: we hit scale-up but pods are stuck in Pending for 30s due to node kubelet pressure.
Alex (SRE): Suggest immediate mitigation: 1) Toggle policy to route heavy requests to fallback lighter variant (redwood-xl-3b-quant) 2) Temporarily increase pool min replicas 3) Pause any non-critical warmups. Can we do (1) now?
Ben (Account Exec): Customer agreed to fallback model for stability, but worried about quality hit. They want 15 min window to test fallback.
Sofia (Sales Eng): OK please coordinate. Raj, can you set fallback routing and patch autoscaler?
Raj (Infra): On it. Patching routing policy now — adding rule: if backend_latency_95 > 8s then route eligible requests to variant=3b-quant.
deploy-bot: routing-policy-updated by raj at 2026-03-20T15:15:12Z
Maya (Oncall): I also raised node drains for two overloaded nodes to force scheduler to move pods. Doing a conservative drain to avoid chasing evictions.
Alex (SRE): After routing change, monitor 95p latency and token consumption. If client still sees failures, we’ll open a dedicated escalation and consider manual pod reschedules.
Sofia (Sales Eng): Customer confirmed fallback traffic started. Early signs: 504s dropping but some timeouts still. They want an RCA and cost impact estimate.
Ben (Account Exec): I’ll prep a short note for them: what we changed, expected quality delta, and next steps.
Raj (Infra): Metrics update: 95p latency dropped from 11.2s -> 4.5s after routing change, token throughput normalized.
Maya (Oncall): Noted one degraded disk on node-7; marking for replacement in maintenance window. Not a blocker for now.
Alex (SRE): Follow-up: we should add a circuit-breaker for KV cache eviction spikes and a proactive autoscale/runbook to suspend warmups under pressure. Filing ticket.
Sofia (Sales Eng): Thanks all. Ben, can you schedule a 30-min sync with the customer in 45 min to walk through changes and share RCA when ready?
Ben (Account Exec): Yup scheduling now.
Sofia (Sales Eng): Leaving this thread open — will update once we have RCA link. :thumbsup:
